packageRules.description: Never bump PyExifTool. Pinned to 0.4.9; 0.5.x breaks metadata extraction.

Never auto-bump these. hdbscan and timezonefinder also have arm64 wheels pinned by URL in requirements.txt. The backend-gpu image runs Python 3.10, but newer releases of these packages drop py3.10, so apps/backend/requirements.txt carries a python_version split (newest on >=3.11, last py3.10-compatible on <3.11). Renovate applies one version to every matching line and collapses the split, breaking the GPU build. Bump manually and keep the <3.11 pin on a py3.10-compatible version: scikit-learn<=1.7.2, timezonefinder<=8.2.0, onnxruntime<=1.23.2.
insightface has no wheels on PyPI; requirements.txt pins wheels built by the prebuilt-wheels workflow next to the PyPI pin. Bump them together by hand and re-run the workflow.

The root package.json is the npm workspace for apps/mobile and packages/*, and pins Expo, expo-router and React to move in lockstep with apps/mobile; packages/* are only consumed by the mobile app. Exact root paths, so apps/frontend and apps/docs manifests are not caught.
Deploy updates are never built by PR CI (the image workflows run on push to dev only), so they must not automerge.
The k8s manifests pin release tags and a Postgres major by hand; a Postgres major refuses to start on an existing data volume. Update them manually with a documented migration.
The GPU image stays on CUDA 12.1.1 / ubuntu22.04 / Python 3.10. Bump by hand only.
A new Ubuntu release swaps the distro Python under the backend base image. Move between LTS releases by hand after a test build.
A Postgres major needs pg_upgrade or dump/restore on existing volumes. Never bump it automatically.
Django 6 requires Python >= 3.12, which the Python 3.10 GPU image cannot install. Stay on the 5.2 LTS until the GPU image moves off 3.10.
typescript-eslint 8 supports TypeScript < 6.1 only; a newer TypeScript fails lint before anything else runs.
Docusaurus, React and MDX majors in the docs site have to move together (Docusaurus pins its React and @mdx-js/react peer ranges), so keep them in one separate PR instead of the docs group.

Frontend majors are split so the safe ones can merge alone. React 19 and Mantine 9 have to ship together (with recharts, which only @mantine/charts uses) and are blocked on replacing react-beautiful-dnd.
zod 4 touches about 70 files; keep it out of the general frontend group.
PR CI does not run the Cypress suite, so keep its updates apart from the app's.
